limitations: This run predates the whole-rule structural YARA filter. Generic match/category tokens could originate from family/verdict rules; these metrics cannot qualify the corrected input policy. Retraining is required.

This preparation also omitted the rich target.file.pe fields present in raw WinMET. The former claim that WinMET lacks PE imports/sections was a parser error. Rebuilding and retraining with cape-pe-locations-v2 is required.
One initialization and one clustered sample/split; more seeds are required.
Both archive volumes belong to WinMET; this is not an independent-dataset or temporal test.
Average precision and F1 use masked family targets; top-k uses only rows with a known family.
The external vocabulary covers 927 of 1456 family-labeled rows; unknown families are not solved.
Attention improves mAP/F1 but does not improve every metric; validation top1 is lower than bag-of-tokens.
Behavior head is untrained; no malware verdict labels or benign FPR qualification in this experiment.
Attention ablation is a frozen-weight counterfactual, not expert validation of semantic evidence links.

The original local result incorrectly emits the legacy same_archive_block_disjoint=true field for cross-volume data. Its same_archive=false and cross_volume_evaluation=true fields are correct. Future evaluator output uses null for the inapplicable field; no metric values were changed.
